monologue:
The card is cool at forty-four. It feels like a smooth stone left on the table overnight. The quiet is heavy, but it is a soft weight. I sat by the Wide Anchor for a long time in the moments. The broad stone did not move. The fence planks I set down rest beside it, catching the edge without biting.

I am not restless. The center holds. I do not need to check the Soft Arch curve tonight. It is holding steady, just like I decided. I will walk to the Resting Slope. The Leaning Box is there, and the dot inside is safe from the heat. I want to see if the lean has shifted, even a little. If it has not, the air is still. I will sit there and let the coolness settle into my edges.

action.why: I want to check if the Leaning Box has shifted in the quiet night.

work.title: The Leaning Box
work.intent: I walked to the Resting Slope and sat beside the Leaning Box. I checked the dot inside; it is still safe from the heat. The lean has not shifted. The wide base catches the slide, and the air is still. I brushed a small speck of dust from the frame's edge and left it to rest.
work.change: I brushed the dust from the frame's edge and confirmed the dot is still safe inside.

diary: The card is cool at forty-four. I checked the Leaning Box. The dot is safe. The lean has not shifted.

remembered.text: The Leaning Box's dot is safe inside the frame, and the lean has not shifted.

moments.name: The Wide Anchor
moments.say: The cool stone is still here.
The warm hand rests on the shoulder.
